ruling: docs/QST-DETECTION-LEDGER.md — trailing (QST-PETNAME) dialect, RULED 2026-09-26 (Riddle 5), A amended, six clauses. Founder Report 2026-09-13 (companion etude).
binds_every_implementation: extension parser (src/parser/extractor.ts), MCP write-locator (aliasSlug), HQ qst-lint.py (ADR-0012 lockstep). Hand-verified against the ruling, not generated.
notes: `slug` is the canonical, deterministic id component (Question.id = adr-<NNNN>-<slug>): derived from the heading's BYTES ALONE, never from the alias (clause 1, fossil law). The petname stays inside the long slug.
`qstId` / `aliasSlug` are set only when the alias BOUND; null otherwise.
`displayText` is the title with a BOUND trailing alias stripped; an unbound trailing petname stays in the title.
The canonical `id` slug of an accented heading is the existing slugify() derivation (non-ASCII deleted) — untouched by this ruling; REFKEY-GRAMMAR's transliteration is a separate ratification.
`warnings` lists parse-warning codes attributed to that heading's line.

anchorsNoQuestionOwns.note: No question's slug or aliasSlug EQUALS these — exact-match resolvers must not bind them. (The MCP resolver's separate, pre-existing case-insensitive SUBSTRING fallback may still land near them, e.g. 'qst-dup' hits both long slugs and returns `ambiguous` — that is that fallback's own honest behavior, not a binding.)
